correctness.rationale: Internal-side controlled phases are local unitaries. After removing them, summing characters on the other side gives the reduced matrix p^{-k} times the indicator that two strings differ by an element of ker(M_A^T). Its all-ones coset blocks yield p^r equal nonzero reduced eigenvalues p^{-r}. An independent exact census used the pole-and-pentagon graph and permutation-expansion determinants instead of the supplied golden-ratio graph and Bareiss determinants. It reproduced all Smith entries for all 2,510 subsets. For balanced subsets the absolute determinants have frequencies 0:392, 1:500, 4:20, 5:12. The exact divisors, not sampling primes, show that only 2 and 5 are exceptional, and reduction and summation give the three listed rank histograms. For the northern five neighbours plus the south pole, order the opposite pentagon and then the north pole on the other side. The cross matrix has upper-left I+P for a five-cycle shift P, an all-ones last column and row off the bottom-right zero, and determinant of magnitude 2*(5/2)=5 by the Schur complement over Q. In characteristic five the five-by-five block is invertible, so exactly one rank unit is lost. The independent census verified the entire determinant-five set equals the prescribed N(v) plus antipode sets. The twelve are labelled six-sets, i.e. six unordered cuts; counting both sides at k=6 is part of the hypothesis, and the table does not count 2,510 unordered cuts.

value.rationale: The natural Platonic graph is a concrete test of how cut entanglement depends on local prime dimension, even with identical unit weights. The table specifies the entire arithmetic cut law for this graph rather than a chosen small slice. It singles out characteristic five and locates every associated defect in a geometric antipodal family, giving a usable benchmark and explicit witnesses without claiming a general protocol or a family theorem.
